clue.text: A waste of time with empty beer glass, nothing to drink

indicators.note: to drink something is to take it in, so the nothing goes inside the other piece

parts.note: someone whose beer glass is empty is pint-less
O is the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A grumble that a pub visit with an empty glass and nothing left to drink is a waste of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to drink' puts O inside PINTLESS, the state of having no pint.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pointless serves no purpose, so it is a waste of time; the phrase works predicatively, as in 'it's pointless'.

clue.text: Conference seeking reconciliation, where seeds may develop in conversation?

indicators.note: words in conversation are spoken, so the phrase is what is heard rather than written

parts.note: pea stalks bear the pods in which the seeds, peas, develop

explanation.surface: Peace negotiations pictured as a place where seeds of agreement may germinate through talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in conversation' signals that PEA STALKS spoken aloud gives PEACE TALKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Peace talks are negotiations between warring sides aimed at ending conflict and reaching a settlement.

clue.text: Suspicion understood by ruthless fictional species on being abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned means dropped, so the word 'on' is taken out of the phrase

parts.note: if Klingons, the warlike aliens of Star Trek, understand something, it is in Klingon

explanation.surface: A suspicion that a merciless alien race from fiction has caught on.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove ON from IN KLINGON; the Klingons are the aggressive warrior race of Star Trek.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkling is a slight hint or vague suspicion of something.

clue.text: See 1
See 16
Flat out, prepare for a fight

parts.note: square can mean level or flat, as a square surface
off means out, as with lights that are off

explanation.surface: An order to drop flat out and then get ready to fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat out' reads as one phrase meaning at full speed, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To square off is to take up a fighting stance facing an opponent.

clue.text: Metal brackets in case for instrument

indicators.note: to bracket something is to enclose it, so the metal goes either side

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron, a metal
in case means if, as a condition

explanation.surface: Metal brackets packed inside a musical instrument case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brackets' looks like a noun for fittings but is the verb meaning encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: A fife is a small high-pitched flute played in military bands.

clue.text: Crack one with line did you say?

indicators.note: a query about what was said signals that the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: a fisher is an angler, someone with a fishing line

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone said a crack was one with a line in it.
explanation.walkthrough: FISHER spoken aloud resembles FISSURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A fissure is a long narrow opening or split, as in rock or ice.

clue.text: Fracas kicking off if hot dog thrown about?

definitions.text: Fracas kicking off if hot dog thrown about?

indicators.note: kicking off means starting, so only the opening letter of fracas is used
thrown about means scattered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A brawl starting when a hot dog gets hurled around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown about' makes OODFIGHT from the clue's 'if hot dog'; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A food fight is a chaotic brawl in which people throw food, like a hot dog, at each other.

clue.text: Gymnastic feat where champion hit the roof

parts.note: to champion a cause is to back it
to hit the roof is to flip, lose one's temper

explanation.surface: A gymnast so explosive that a champion's leap hits the ceiling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit the roof' suggests a high jump but means losing one's temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A backflip is a backwards somersault performed in gymnastics.

clue.text: Failing to push for result

indicators.note: failing suggests breaking down, so the letters fall apart and are reordered

explanation.surface: Being penalised for not pushing hard enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Failing' rearranges TO PUSH.
explanation.definitionFit: The upshot is the eventual outcome or conclusion of something.

clue.text: Extraordinary student I observed in class

indicators.note: observed in means seen within, so the I sits inside the other word

parts.note: a genus is a class in biological classification

explanation.surface: A pupil reporting an exceptional student spotted in their class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'class' is a classroom on the surface but a biological category here.
explanation.definitionFit: A genius is a person of exceptional intellect, such as a brilliant pupil.

clue.text: Same fur wound around friends initially warming couple?

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the initial
wound, as in twisted, means the letters are wrapped into a new order
initially means the first letter of friends is taken

explanation.surface: Identical fur wrapped around companions to keep a pair warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' rearranges SAME FUR into EARMUFS, which goes around F from 'friends initially'.
explanation.definitionFit: Earmuffs come as a pair of padded covers worn to keep the ears warm.

clue.text: Complex way to end communication?

explanation.surface: A complicated method of ending a conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: A hang-up is an emotional complex, and hanging up is how a phone call ends.

clue.text: Love affair within a limit

indicators.note: within means the affair sits inside the other letters

parts.note: a ration is a fixed limit or allowance
a do is a party or affair

explanation.surface: A love affair kept within bounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affair' suggests romance but means a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep love and devotion.

clue.text: Good player after women times header in effortless turn

parts.note: pi is short for pious, meaning good
a roue is a rake, a player who chases women
T stands for time, so times gives two

indicators.note: header means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A sports report: a fine player, after a woman's header, turns with ease.
explanation.walkthrough: PI (pious) is a crossword convention for good.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirouette is a spin on one foot, a ballet turn.

clue.text: Very old cardinal put on clothes

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here, dresses or wraps around

parts.note: to put on a play is to stage it
one is a cardinal number

explanation.surface: An elderly cardinal of the Church putting on his robes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinal' suggests a churchman but is a cardinal number; 'clothes' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Stone Age describes something extremely primitive or old-fashioned, from the prehistoric era.

clue.text: Keep something hideous, pornographic magazines perhaps for online literary creation?

parts.note: to hog is to keep for oneself
a wart is an ugly growth
pornographic publications might be called the sex press

explanation.surface: A lurid instruction to hog sleazy magazines for an internet book project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'online' suggests the internet but means running on rails.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hogwarts Express is the train in the Harry Potter books, a fictional creation that runs on a line.

clue.text: See 23
Dear little couple supporting society

indicators.note: in a down answer, supporting means the later pieces sit below

parts.note: wee is Scots for little
to tie is to couple or join

explanation.surface: A sweet small pair propping up high society.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'supporting' means the later pieces sit below the society letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetie and dear are both affectionate terms of address.

clue.text: Tex-Mex food for another journey, it's tacos apparently for starters

indicators.note: for starters means the opening letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: Seeking more Tex-Mex for another trip, since apparently tacos are just the beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: A fajita is a Tex-Mex dish of grilled strips of meat wrapped in a tortilla.

clue.text: Throne issue for PM and POTUS?

parts.note: a john is slang for a toilet, jokingly called the throne
issue means offspring, as a son

explanation.surface: A succession problem for both a prime minister and a US president.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris Johnson was a British prime minister; Andrew and Lyndon Johnson were US presidents.
explanation.definitionFit: Johnson is the surname shared by a UK prime minister and two American presidents.

clue.text: Work on hand, one caught between stools?

indicators.note: between means placed inside the other word

parts.note: manure is animal droppings, stools
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A worker on the job falls between two stools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stools' are seats in the idiom but droppings here.
explanation.definitionFit: A manicure is cosmetic treatment of the hands and fingernails.

clue.text: Cutting hem back, I see a soft fabric

indicators.note: cutting means splitting into, so the inner letters go inside
back means the word for hem is read in reverse

parts.note: a hem is an edge, or rim
oh is an exclamation like I see

explanation.surface: A seamstress trimming a hem, noting a soft cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses RIM to MIR, which OHA cuts into.
explanation.definitionFit: Mohair is a soft yarn or fabric made from the hair of the Angora goat.

clue.text: Fish with second fish

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a second
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: One fish paired with another.
explanation.definitionFit: A moray is a kind of eel, a sea fish.

clue.text: Girl over here about to quickly mix drink

parts.note: Iris is a girl's name

indicators.note: about means around, so the call surrounds the mixing word

parts.note: hey is a call to attract attention, like over here
to whisk is to mix quickly

explanation.surface: A girl calling for a drink to be mixed quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish whiskey is a spirit distilled in Ireland.

clue.text: Protest: gather it is audible?

indicators.note: audible means heard, so the phrase is taken as sound

parts.note: to gather it is to pick it

explanation.surface: A protester asking whether gathering something can be heard.
explanation.walkthrough: PICK IT spoken aloud gives PICKET.
explanation.definitionFit: A picket is a protest outside a workplace, typically during a strike.

clue.text: How to get tips for cooking equipment

parts.note: read as an instruction, the answer says turn the word spit around, which makes the word tips

explanation.surface: Advice on earning gratuities by way of kitchen gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnspit is a rotating rod for roasting meat over a fire.

clue.text: Tip of little finger sliced off, black

indicators.note: tip of points to the first letter of the finger word as the one removed
sliced off means cut away, so that letter is removed

parts.note: pinky is a name for the little finger

explanation.surface: A gruesome accident: a fingertip cut off, leaving it black.
explanation.definitionFit: Inky means as dark as ink, so jet black.

clue.text: What inspires remarkably popular leader of community totally

indicators.note: inspires means breathes in, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: eh is a query meaning what
very means remarkably
in means popular or fashionable

indicators.note: leader of means the first letter of community

explanation.surface: Asking what motivates a well-liked community leader so thoroughly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspires' puts VERYINC inside EH.
explanation.definitionFit: Every inch is an idiom meaning entirely or in every respect.
